fingerprints.title: Sunday, March 15
fingerprints.intro_excerpt:
Woke up late today. The rain against the window made it impossible to
get out of bed before ten. Made coffee the way I like it — pour-over,
medium grind, exactly 200 degrees. Mom called while I was still in my
pajamas. She wants me to visit next month.
Spent the afternoon at the bookstore on Powell. Picked up a copy of
Anna Karenina I will probably never finish and a used travel guide to
Japan. Sat in the cafe for two hours just reading and people-watching.
An elderly couple sat across from me sharing a single pastry and
speaking what sounded like Portuguese. I want that kind of slow,
unhurried companionship someday.
Made pasta for dinner. Nothing fancy — garlic, olive oil, red pepper
flakes, the last of the parmesan. Watched half of a documentary about
deep-sea creatures before falling asleep on the couch. Not a productive
day, but a good one.

fingerprints.title: Building Reliable Postgres Replication
fingerprints.intro_excerpt:
Postgres replication is the backbone of any production database deployment.
Without it, you are one hardware failure away from a very bad day.
Streaming replication copies the entire WAL stream to a standby. It is simple
and battle-tested but gives you an exact physical copy — no filtering, no
transformation. Logical replication operates at the table level and lets you
select which tables to replicate, transform data, or even replicate between
different Postgres major versions.
Replication slots can fill your disk if a standby falls behind. Always monitor
`pg_stat_replication` and set `max_slot_wal_keep_size`. Connection drops during
heavy write loads can cause the standby to fall behind faster than it can catch
up — tune `wal_sender_timeout` and `max_wal_senders` accordingly.

fingerprints.title: Q4 Product Strategy Notes
fingerprints.intro_excerpt:
The product has strong retention among power users but acquisition has
plateaued. Our CAC is ~$45 and LTV is ~$180 for the core segment. The
onboarding flow is the biggest drop-off point — 62% of signups never
complete the first project setup.
The data points to three high-leverage moves this quarter:
1. **Onboarding overhaul.** Simplify the first-run experience from 7 steps
to 3. Add contextual tooltips and a progress indicator. Target: reduce
drop-off from 62% to 40%.
2. **Freemium pricing test.** Launch a limited free tier with 3 projects
and 1GB storage. Gate collaboration and analytics behind the Pro plan.
Monitor conversion rate over 60 days.
3. **API-first strategy.** Expose the core workflow engine as a REST API
so larger accounts can integrate with their existing tools. This opens
a high-ACV enterprise segment we have not yet addressed.
Weekly active users, project completion rate, time-to-first-project,
Pro plan conversion rate, API token provisioning count.
